rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: RE-JUDGED FRESH 2026-07-26, VERDICT CHANGED FROM BLOCKING TO NON-BLOCKING — full independent re-analysis, not a deferral to the maintainer's stated reasoning. On the strict letter of §16, the finding still holds: lines 24-27 ('Read the diff and push back on a line') carry a genuine forcing function ('push back... quote the line and say why') entirely in body prose, no {{prompt:}} fence, named as one of the exercise's two core disciplines in 'The point' (line 9), Theme 4 in the maintainer block, and this file's own Leap Test #2 ('Pushes back on at least one line in a diff before merging'). That much matches the prior judge pass. But §56 ('Engineer-audience audit fixes default to body callout... reserve forcing-function fixes for actions that gate downstream correctness AND have a non-recoverable failure mode') governs the FIX SHAPE for exactly this kind of finding, and on independent investigation (not the maintainer's cited reasoning — found separately via git log and a sibling-file read) three pieces of evidence the prior judge pass did not have in view all point to 'recoverable': (1) a REAL cohort incident, not a hypothetical — commit 304f061 ('Cohort 07:14:31Z asked for a pre-made prompt at the diff push-back step') — was answered by adding the exact explanatory sentence now in the file ('Your own wording matters. No pre-made prompt for the pushback... so the words you reach for are yours'); no recurrence is logged since. That is field evidence the recovery path already works, stronger than an untested sim trace. (2) compound-and-close.md carries the training's own precedent for this identical move-family: its 'Push back where the summary misreads' beat is ALSO unfenced body prose, and its maintainer block explicitly logs it as Accept-with-mitigation per §50/§51 ('body prose immediately below the prompt... IS the engagement step'). Per §16's own sub-rule 9b (progression-with-variations — same move recurs across the arc, never scripted twice the same way), a fenced prompt here while the Ex3 instance of the same discipline stays unfenced would itself be an inconsistency, not a fix. (3) Under check_slides.md's deck model, '## Read the diff and push back on a line' is not buried body prose a speed-runner skips — it is the section's own slide title, command-verb-led, self-carrying per check_slides.md §6. The §16 'read prompt-only, ignore body' diagnostic was written for forcing functions hidden inside paragraphs under a generic header; it under-weights how visible a `##` title is in the actual delivery surface. Net: the miss is recoverable within the diagnostic's own 'notice and recover in under a minute' bar — via the slide-title command verb alone, reinforced by live trainer narration in AE101's default in-room delivery (training-architecture.md: cohort delivery does not install or depend on self-study tooling; in-room is the default, not an edge case), and backstopped by a second, independent attempt at the same discipline 15 minutes later in Ex3. The persona trace's confusion_flags entry (phase 1, unchanged across regenerations) does not show the persona actually confused in-room — persona_action has them performing the push-back cleanly; the flag is the judge's own structural-risk note about a hypothetical self-study-only read, correctly named as a residual risk, not an observed failure.

The one open item is documentation parity, not design: this file's maintainer block should carry an explicit Accept-with-mitigation note mirroring compound-and-close.md's (cite §50/§51, name the cohort-incident history and the header-self-carries argument), so the next audit cycle doesn't have to re-derive this reasoning from scratch and re-flag a closed question. Downgraded from blocking because the maintainer's no-fence call is independently defensible on evidence this pass gathered directly (git history + sibling file), not merely on the maintainer's asserted design intent.
